trigger: Fractional propagation did not transfer from SMACS to SPT, while spatial extent repeatedly dominated normalized-map parameter impacts.
question: Can an ordinary Poisson field with one universal symmetry-gated baryonic broadening scale improve raw image-plane consistency in both clusters?

formula.interpretation: B_w is the observed member-light map convolved to one universal physical width w; no fractional propagator is used.

selection.rule: For each candidate fit one positive amplitude per cluster on its frozen calibration subfamilies. Select minimum equal-cluster mean calibration image-plane RMS; score both frozen held-out cohorts without refitting width, fraction, or amplitudes.

cross_domain.Solar: H=0 in the one-source limit, so the broad component is absent and the unsmoothed ordinary field remains.
cross_domain.SPARC: Q90=0 for deprojected axisymmetric profiles, so broadening changes all 175 rotation curves by exactly zero.
cross_domain.scope: The physical widths describe the cluster member-field response only where the same symmetry gate is active.

claim_limits: F160W member light is only a proxy for stellar baryons and omits gas, ICL, and mass-to-light variation.
One amplitude per cluster is still calibrated, so absolute strength is not universal or predicted.
The same raw positions used in P0575-P0577 are reused; this compares a new formula family rather than providing new data.
Linearized image-plane residuals are not full nonlinear root finding.
A fixed physical width is phenomenological and not derived from a covariant field equation.
